name: Piper PA-31 Navajo / Chieftain
variants: (PA-31T Cheyenne turboprops are a separate family)
summary: Cabin-class piston twin widely used by commuter, charter and freight operators, especially the stretched Chieftain.

wings: Low wing with tapered outer panels
engines: Two flat-six engines in long nacelles with baggage lockers at the rear
fuselage: Large unpressurized cabin with big squarish windows
Rear airstair/split door on the left

tellTales: Cabin-class piston twin with large squarish windows
Swept fin with dorsal strake above a low tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The 340/414/421 have a rounder pressurized fuselage with small rounded windows; the Navajo has larger square windows.
The King Air has turboprop nacelles with exhaust stacks; the Navajo has piston nacelles without stacks.
The Seneca is smaller with a short nose and a single-engine-style cabin; the Navajo is a larger cabin-class twin with a long nose.
The Cheyenne has smoother turbine nacelles, prop spinners and a long pointed nose; the Navajo has piston-engine cowlings and a blunter nose.
The PA-42 Cheyenne III/400 has a T-tail and turboprop nacelles; the Navajo has a low horizontal tail and piston-engine cowlings.
The 402 has a straighter-sided cabin and, on early models, big wingtip tanks; the Navajo has a tapered wing with plain tips and a dorsal strake on the fin.
